issues.legal_issue: A daughter is entitled to equal rights in coparcenary property under the amended succession law when a partition suit has reached only the preliminary-decree stage and no legally completed partition occurred before the statutory cutoff.
material_facts: The dispute concerned coparcenary property in a partition suit brought by a son against his father, brother, and sisters.
A preliminary decree determining shares was passed and later amended, but no final decree partitioning the property had been passed.
The amendment came into force while the proceedings for the final decree were pending.
The sisters sought equal shares under the amendment, and the property had not been partitioned by a registered instrument or court decree before the statutory cutoff.
issues.conclusion: The sisters were entitled to equal shares in the coparcenary property under the amended law; the preliminary decree could not deprive them of those rights because no partition had been completed before the statutory cutoff.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as substituted by the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005, gives a daughter the same coparcenary rights and liabilities as a son. Under Section 6(5) and its Explanation, the exclusion for an earlier partition applies to a partition effected before the cutoff by a duly registered partition deed or a court decree. A preliminary decree declaring shares does not itself complete partition. The Court applied S. Sai Reddy v. S. Narayana Reddy, which held that daughters could claim the benefit of a beneficial amendment before final partition, and relied on the principles concerning preliminary decrees in Phoolchand v. Gopal Lal.

rule.if: partition_suit and daughter_of_coparcener and coparcenary_property and amendment_applies_before_final_partition and not completed_partition_before_cutoff

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit to partition family property.
predicates.daughter_of_coparcener: A woman claiming a share is the daughter of a member of the coparcenary.
predicates.coparcenary_property: The property in dispute is coparcenary property.
predicates.amendment_applies_before_final_partition: The amended rule took effect while the partition proceeding remained incomplete.
predicates.completed_partition_before_cutoff: The property was partitioned before the relevant cutoff by a legally recognized completed partition.

issues.definition: When a daughter claims coparcenary property in a partition suit, the amendment applies before final partition, and no completed partition occurred before the cutoff, she has equal coparcenary rights.

issues.legal_issue: A court may revise or replace an unappealed preliminary decree in a partition suit when a supervening change affects the parties’ shares and the final decree has not been passed.
material_facts: A preliminary decree determined the parties’ shares in the partition suit, and no appeal was brought against it.
The final decree had not been passed when the amended succession law gave the sisters rights affecting the shares.
The trial court allowed the sisters’ application to have their shares redetermined before final partition.
The High Court set aside that order on the ground that the final decree had to conform to the existing preliminary decree.
issues.conclusion: The trial court had power to redetermine the shares and amend or pass another preliminary decree before the final decree; the absence of an appeal from the earlier preliminary decree did not prevent that action.
issues.legal_principle: Order XX Rule 18 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs partition decrees. A partition suit continues after a preliminary decree until the final decree is passed, and a court may amend that decree or pass a further preliminary decree when an intervening event requires a change in shares. Section 97 of the Code does not bar that power merely because no appeal was filed against the preliminary decree. The Court relied on Phoolchand v. Gopal Lal and S. Sai Reddy v. S. Narayana Reddy.

rule.if: partition_suit and preliminary_decree_passed and final_decree_not_passed and intervening_event_changes_shares and preliminary_decree_not_appealed

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit to partition property.
predicates.preliminary_decree_passed: The court has issued a preliminary decree determining the parties’ shares.
predicates.final_decree_not_passed: The court has not yet issued the final decree completing the partition.
predicates.intervening_event_changes_shares: An event occurring after the preliminary decree changes the parties’ respective shares.
predicates.preliminary_decree_not_appealed: No party appealed the preliminary decree.

issues.definition: In a partition suit, an intervening event that changes shares before the final decree allows the court to modify an unappealed preliminary decree.
